Photoreal cinematic live-action, Warm high-summer palette of gold ripe wheat, red road dust and deep green pine, hard blue shadow under a clear bleached sky; the Utah valley and Salt Lake City, June 1860; American frontier, sunlight and lamplight only., 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:04. The shot begins from <Picture 1>: a close shot insert at the mustang's flank in the press: the horse's dusty shoulder and barrel, a long polished horn swinging in across it, dust in the hair of the hide, a boot and stirrup at the top of the frame. The camera is low at the height of the horse's belly, an arm's length from the flank, a 90mm lens. The overhead sun stripes the flank through the dust. At the first frame The horse's flank fills the LEFT two thirds and the horn crosses the middle band. The camera pushes in on the flank across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth as the long horn comes across and knocks against the horse's barrel, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 the hide flinches away under it, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him Six wild-looking herdsmen on ponies ride the flanks of the drove at a normal walking pace swinging coiled ropes, and two more sit their horses at the corral rail watching the road., from 00:00 to 00:04. By 00:04, the flank and the horn fill the frame edge to edge with the top edge across the stirrup leather.
